newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC ministers seek wider role for private sector.
newsitem.headline: APEC ministers seek wider role for private sector.

text.p: APEC trade ministers ended a two-day meeting on Friday, urging the private sector to be more involved in achieving the group's goal of freeing trade within the region.

"The ministers welcome the increasing participation of the private sector and encourage greater business involvement in the APEC SME Action Programme," said a statement issued by ministers attending a meeting on Small and Medium Enterprises (SME).

The Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum ministers meeting agreed on US$700,000 in new economic and technical cooperation projects that they would undertake to accelerate the development of small businesses. The meeting, one in a series this year, was held on Cebu, a central Philippine island.
Also on Friday, businessmen held a meeting parallel to the ministerial forum to discuss their problems in doing business in the Asia Pacific region.

The businessmen, in a report to the ministers, said tough visa rules were one of their main problems in doing business. They suggested that APEC members introduce multiple-entry business visas granted for five years.
The businessmen said governments should also reduce the cost of information technology so that smaller companies could access information about other markets over the Internet.

Noboru Endo, head of the Japanese delegation to the ministerial meeting, said private sector participation was essential for APEC to meet its goal of freeing trade and investment in the region by 2010 for rich countries and by 2020 for poorer ones.

"I believe what we need to bring about in the future is that industry representatives as well as representatives of support groups...be part of APEC meetings and possibly in the future to include their participation in the meeting of leaders as well," Endo said.
APEC leaders, including U.S. President Bill Clinton, are to attend the forum's annual summit in the Philippines in November.

APEC members are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore, and the United States.
